summary: Eight major events in six weeks. Scan the one-line summaries; open only what matters.

events.title: Deramiocel for Duchenne cardiomyopathy
events.trigger: FDA's cell-and-gene-therapy committee votes July 29 after reviewing BLA 125842; the final action date is August 22. The committee packet is due no later than two business days before the meeting.
events.implication: Deramiocel is Capricor's value-defining asset and would be the first therapy aimed specifically at DMD cardiomyopathy. HOPE-3 met its PUL v2.0 primary endpoint and key LVEF cardiac endpoint, but the committee must still accept efficacy durability, manufacturing comparability, and the cell-therapy package.
events.white_swan: A clearly positive vote followed by approval with a broad DMD-cardiomyopathy label and no launch-blocking manufacturing conditions. That validates the platform, activates the Nippon Shinyaku commercialization path, and can reopen the prior 52-week high near $40.
events.base_case: The committee acknowledges efficacy but splits on durability, endpoint interpretation, or CMC. FDA either approves with a narrower label/post-marketing burden or delays for additional manufacturing commitments.
events.black_swan: A negative vote or Complete Response Letter citing inadequate evidence, product consistency, or inspection/CMC deficiencies. Because deramiocel dominates CAPR's valuation, the stock can revisit single digits rather than trade like a diversified biotech.
events.why_mispriced: The clinical headline is positive, but the regulatory event is actually two-dimensional: efficacy and the manufacturability of an allogeneic cell product. FDA briefing documents can change the probability tree before the vote, while the stock already sits far above its $4.30 52-week low.
events.magnitude: At July 24 marks, the September 18 $20 straddle was about $17.25, roughly ±87% around $19.75. The expiry includes extra time and spreads were wide, so this is a volatility bracket—not a fair-value target.
events.action: Read FDA and sponsor briefing books line by line when posted. Build a matrix for efficacy population, PUL/LVEF effect, missing data, durability, CMC comparability, inspection status, vote wording, and label scope.
events.invalidation: FDA postpones the meeting or extends the action date; either change breaks the current timing and makes the quoted option bracket stale.
events.watch: FDA briefing-document tone, exact voting question, manufacturing/inspection language, panel vote, and whether labeling discussions are disclosed before August 22.
events.plain_summary: FDA advisers vote July 29 on CAPR’s main heart treatment. The final FDA decision is due August 22.
events.plain_good: Approval could move the stock back toward its old high near $40.
events.plain_bad: Rejection could cut the stock into single digits.
events.plain_watch: Wait for FDA briefing documents, the panel vote, and any manufacturing concerns.

events.title: RP1 plus nivolumab in anti-PD-1-failed melanoma
events.trigger: FDA's cell-and-gene-therapy committee reviews BLA 125827 on July 30, followed by the August 2 action date. This is a repeat regulatory attempt after prior Complete Response Letters.
events.implication: REPL is trying to convert a 34% response rate and 24.8-month median duration into accelerated approval using a single-arm program. The key question is not whether responses occurred; it is whether FDA accepts their attribution, durability, historical-control framework, and RP1's contribution over nivolumab.
events.white_swan: A positive vote and accelerated approval with a workable confirmatory-trial requirement. That turns REPL from a repeatedly rejected developer into a commercial oncology company and validates the oncolytic-immunotherapy platform.
events.base_case: A divided committee: durable responses look real, but FDA demands tighter evidence on contribution and control selection. A narrow approval, delayed action, or onerous confirmatory requirement produces a less explosive outcome.
events.black_swan: Another negative vote or CRL because the uncontrolled dataset cannot establish contribution or because FDA still finds the evidence uninterpretable. A third failure would damage both RP1 and platform credibility and could send the stock back toward the post-CRL zone near its $1.50 52-week low.
events.why_mispriced: The same 34% response statistic supports both narratives: extraordinary activity in refractory melanoma and selection/attribution risk in a single-arm study. A repeated-review setup also makes precedent less useful than the actual July 30 voting question.
events.magnitude: The August 7 $10 straddle marked about $6.05, implying roughly ±62% around $9.82 and a crude $3.77–$15.87 bracket. Bid/ask spreads were enormous; use only as confirmation that the market sees a binary event.
events.action: Compare sponsor and FDA analyses of evaluable population, independent review, complete-response rate, duration, prior anti-PD-1 exposure, nivolumab contribution, and confirmatory-trial feasibility.
events.invalidation: FDA delays the committee or action date, or publishes briefing documents showing the vote is not on approvability/contribution.
events.watch: FDA briefing books, vote wording, panel discussion of historical controls, and any requirement for randomized evidence before approval.
events.plain_summary: FDA advisers vote July 30 on REPL’s cancer treatment. A final decision is due August 2 after earlier rejections.
events.plain_good: Approval would turn REPL into a commercial cancer-drug company.
events.plain_bad: Another rejection could send shares back toward their post-rejection lows.
events.plain_watch: Watch the FDA briefing documents and the exact question the panel must vote on.

events.title: BlueBirds 11, 12, and 13 launch on one SpaceX mission
events.trigger: AST SpaceMobile says BlueBirds 11–13 are targeted to launch together in the first half of August. The exact launch day remains subject to SpaceX range scheduling and weather. Three satellites on one rocket concentrate both deployment upside and mission risk.
events.implication: The launch is a concrete test of ASTS production cadence and constellation scaling—not another slide-deck milestone. The market needs successful insertion, array deployment, initial contact, and evidence that the company can repeat the cadence.
events.white_swan: On-time launch, clean separation, all three arrays deploy, and initial telemetry supports a credible path toward continuous service. One mission adds three satellites and validates manufacturing throughput.
events.base_case: The launch succeeds but schedule slips within August or commissioning takes weeks. The operational milestone is real, while commercial coverage and cash burn remain the valuation bottlenecks.
events.black_swan: Launch failure, partial deployment, loss of contact, or another material delay. With three satellites concentrated on one mission and ASTS still pre-scale, a single failure can reset network timing and financing needs.
events.why_mispriced: ASTS is already a $22.3B company and has traded between $36 and $134 in the last year. Bulls price a communications platform; this event still carries launch-vehicle, deployment, and constellation-cadence risk in one concentrated payload.
events.magnitude: At July 24 marks, the August 14 $55 straddle was about $12.70, roughly ±22.6% around $56.23 and a crude $43.53–$68.93 bracket. OI was 102 calls/390 puts and spreads were meaningful; this is volatility evidence, not a target.
events.action: Track the exact launch notice, weather/range updates, launch webcast, separation confirmation, first contact, solar/array deployment, and initial in-orbit commissioning. Do not call the mission successful at liftoff.
events.invalidation: The company moves the mission beyond September 5 or separates the three satellites into a different manifest; either breaks the current event definition and option expiry match.
events.watch: Company launch-date update, SpaceX manifest, launch-window slips, payload integration, post-separation telemetry, array deployment, and any financing announcement around the mission.

sources.label: AST SpaceMobile press releases — June 23 launch announcement

events.plain_summary: ASTS plans to launch three satellites together in early August.
events.plain_good: A clean launch and deployment would keep the network rollout on track.
events.plain_bad: A failure or long delay could reset the rollout and increase financing needs.
events.plain_watch: Do not stop at liftoff; wait for all three satellites to connect and deploy their arrays.

events.title: Magnetics ramp and first H2 commercial-revenue checkpoint
events.trigger: MP reports Q2 on August 6. The discontinuity is not EPS; it is whether management converts second-half magnet-revenue guidance into a dated production and shipment ramp at Independence while maintaining Mountain Pass execution and funding the buildout.
events.implication: MP is a strategic U.S. rare-earth and magnet supply-chain asset, but the stock needs proof that government-supported capacity becomes repeatable commercial output. The call can move the market if production timing, yield, customer acceptance, or capital intensity changes.
events.white_swan: Management confirms first commercial magnet shipments and revenue on schedule, quantifies throughput and yield, and shows contracted demand supporting a credible ramp without surprise financing.
events.base_case: Magnet revenue still starts in H2, but contribution is small and ramp details remain qualitative. Government support limits downside while execution proof remains deferred.
events.black_swan: Independence commissioning or customer qualification slips, capex rises, Mountain Pass economics weaken, or new financing is needed before meaningful magnet cash flow. The strategic narrative remains intact but duration expands.
events.why_mispriced: MP closed July 24 at its 52-week low of $41.12 after trading above $100. Policy support is visible; factory yield, qualification, shipment cadence, and cash conversion are not. The event is lower-confidence than an FDA date but adds genuine industrial exposure.
events.magnitude: The August 7 $40 straddle marked about $5.13, implying roughly ±12.4% around $41.29 and a crude $36.16–$46.41 bracket. Call OI was only 7 and spreads were wide; treat this as noisy event-vol evidence.
events.action: Ignore headline EPS. Track magnet tons and units, qualified lines, shipment date, customer acceptance, realized pricing, Pentagon support mechanics, capex, cash burn, Mountain Pass output, and 2026 revenue guidance.
events.invalidation: MP preannounces shipment timing or materially changes the August 6 event. If management gives no bounded H2 milestone, downgrade this from catalyst to ordinary earnings.
events.watch: Independence commissioning, first commercial shipment, yield and throughput, customer qualification, magnet revenue recognition, capex, cash runway, and government-contract milestones.
events.plain_summary: On August 6, MP should say whether its U.S. magnet factory has started shipping products and earning revenue.
events.plain_good: On-time shipments would prove the new factory is working.
events.plain_bad: Delays, higher costs, or new financing would push profits further away.
events.plain_watch: Ignore headline earnings; watch shipment timing, factory output, costs, and cash burn.

events.title: Final determination in crafting-machine import case 337-TA-1426
events.trigger: The USITC extended its target date to August 13 for the final determination in Cricut’s Section 337 case over competing crafting machines. The remedy can include general or limited exclusion orders and cease-and-desist orders against infringing imports.
events.implication: CRCT’s connected-machine hardware seeds its higher-margin subscription and materials ecosystem. A meaningful import remedy could protect machine pricing and installed-base economics; a narrow remedy leaves low-cost competitive pressure largely intact.
events.white_swan: The Commission affirms infringement and grants broad, enforceable exclusion and cease-and-desist relief covering the key competing products. Hardware pricing and ecosystem retention gain a defensible legal moat.
events.base_case: Cricut wins, but relief is respondent- or product-specific and competitors redesign around the patents. The legal result helps at the margin without changing slow category demand.
events.black_swan: No violation, patents narrowed or invalidated, or relief is too limited to matter. Legal spend produces no moat while machine and accessory competition continues.
events.why_mispriced: CRCT is a profitable sub-$1B consumer platform trading near the lower end of its 52-week range, so the market may treat the ITC case as legal noise. The real value depends on remedy breadth, customs enforceability, and whether competitors can redesign—not the headline word “win.”
events.magnitude: A defensible option-implied move is unavailable: the August $5 options had zero bids and essentially no put OI. Use the $3.74–$6.93 52-week range and remedy economics, not displayed option marks.
events.action: Read the final determination and exclusion-order text. Map covered products, patent claims, named respondents, bond during presidential review, carve-outs, and redesign paths before treating the result as commercially meaningful.
events.invalidation: The Commission extends the target date again, the parties settle, or the final remedy is published before August 13.
events.watch: Commission docket, exclusion-order breadth, presidential-review period, Customs enforcement language, respondent redesigns, and Cricut’s comments on hardware/subscription economics.
events.plain_summary: On August 13, a U.S. agency should decide whether Cricut can block imports of competing craft machines.
events.plain_good: A broad import ban could protect Cricut’s pricing and subscription business.
events.plain_bad: A narrow win or loss would leave cheap competition in place.
events.plain_watch: Read which products are actually blocked and whether competitors can redesign around the ruling.

events.title: CrossCountry Mortgage cash acquisition closing window
events.trigger: TWO shareholders approved CrossCountry Mortgage’s cash merger on July 2. The company says closing remains on track for August, subject to remaining state regulatory approvals and customary conditions. Approved consideration is $12.00 cash per share.
events.implication: This is merger-arbitrage, not a growth catalyst. The key variables are final regulatory clearances, exact closing date, deal consideration, and whether any remaining dividend or competing-bid economics explain trading around the $12 cash price.
events.white_swan: All remaining state approvals arrive, the deal closes promptly at $12, and holders capture any contractually permitted incremental distribution or favorable settlement mechanics. A renewed superior proposal would be the true upside tail.
events.base_case: The deal closes in August at the contracted $12. With shares around $12.11 on July 24, ordinary closing alone offers little or negative gross spread before dividends, borrow, taxes, and timing.
events.black_swan: A regulator blocks or delays closing, CCM fails a condition, or the agreement breaks. TWO reprices toward standalone mortgage-REIT value; its 52-week low was $8.78 and the downside dwarfs the visible spread.
events.why_mispriced: The price sat slightly above the stated cash consideration, so this is not a free arbitrage. The market may be pricing dividend mechanics, residual rival-bid optionality, or stale microstructure. Every cent of consideration must be reconciled before acting.
events.magnitude: The September $12 straddle marked about $0.15, only ±1.2% around $12.11. That tiny bracket reflects deal anchoring, while the true broken-deal downside is discontinuous and not captured by symmetric volatility.
events.action: Reconcile the definitive merger agreement, approved $12 consideration, dividend treatment, final state approvals, termination rights, closing conditions, and current price. Do not trade off the press-release headline alone.
events.invalidation: A definitive closing date, completed merger, amended consideration, superior proposal, termination, or delay beyond September 5 supersedes the current event window.
events.watch: Remaining regulatory approvals, closing certificate, dividend adjustments, CCM financing, termination-date language, UWMC activity, and any new 8-K.
events.plain_summary: TWO expects its $12-per-share cash buyout to close in August. Shares were already near $12.11.
events.plain_good: The deal closes as planned, but there is little obvious upside at the current price.
events.plain_bad: A delay or broken deal could send shares toward standalone value near $8.78.
events.plain_watch: Watch final approvals, the exact closing date, and any dividend adjustment.

events.title: DTX401 gene therapy for GSDIa
events.trigger: Priority-review action on one-time AAV8 gene therapy DTX401 for glycogen storage disease type Ia, where no pharmacologic treatment addresses the underlying cause.
events.implication: Phase 3 patients reduced daily cornstarch use 41.3% versus 10.3% on placebo at week 48 while maintaining glucose control (p<0.0001). FDA must still clear AAV safety, durability, CMC, and label questions.
events.white_swan: Approval with a broad eligible population, manageable monitoring, and no restrictive safety language. It creates a first disease-modifying GSDIa therapy and validates RARE's liver-directed gene-therapy engine after sector-wide skepticism.
events.base_case: Approval with conservative monitoring/eligibility and a deliberate launch. Strong trial statistics support efficacy, but rare-disease identification and gene-therapy logistics slow revenue realization.
events.black_swan: CRL or delay for CMC, vector safety, durability, or inspection issues despite the efficacy win. The rejection would contaminate confidence in RARE's second September gene-therapy decision as well as DTX401.
events.why_mispriced: The efficacy endpoint looks unusually clean, so the residual tail risk is mostly non-efficacy FDA risk. Options price a huge move because the September expiry also captures the separate UX111 PDUFA after this brief's window.
events.magnitude: The September 18 $27.50 straddle marked about $15.15, roughly ±56% around $26.90. This overstates the isolated August 23 event because the same expiry includes another RARE PDUFA on September 19 and spreads were wide.
events.action: Separate efficacy probability from CMC/inspection risk. Check label population, steroid/immunosuppression regimen, durability language, liver safety, post-marketing studies, and launch capacity.
events.invalidation: PDUFA extension or confirmation that an inspection/CMC issue will move the action outside the window.
events.watch: FDA action timing, label breadth, safety monitoring, rare-pediatric voucher status, launch timing, and read-through to UX111.
events.plain_summary: FDA is due to decide August 23 on RARE’s one-time gene therapy for a rare liver disease.
events.plain_good: Approval would validate the drug and RARE’s gene-therapy platform.
events.plain_bad: A delay or rejection would hurt this drug and confidence in RARE’s next program.
events.plain_watch: Watch label limits, safety requirements, manufacturing issues, and launch timing.

events.title: LEVEL Phase 3 oral levosimendan in PH-HFpEF
events.trigger: TENX says topline from the registrational LEVEL trial will arrive in August before a late-breaking European Society of Cardiology presentation on August 29. More than 230 patients were enrolled.
events.implication: LEVEL tests TNX-103 in pulmonary hypertension with heart failure and preserved ejection fraction, an area without an approved therapy. The single-asset valuation means the primary efficacy result, safety, and FDA path dominate the equity.
events.white_swan: Statistically persuasive improvement on the prespecified exercise-capacity endpoint, coherent secondary endpoints, and clean safety, followed by an ESC dataset that supports registration and partnership interest.
events.base_case: A nominally positive primary endpoint with mixed secondary endpoints or modest effect size. The program advances, but FDA may still require the planned second Phase 3 study and the valuation rerates less than the option market implies.
events.black_swan: Primary-endpoint miss, clinically trivial effect, safety signal, or a data delay past ESC. For a roughly $386 million single-asset company, that can erase most development value and force financing on ugly terms.
events.why_mispriced: The September options imply an absurdly wide range, but that does not mean the binary is understood. The crucial distinction is 'statistically positive' versus 'registration-quality effect with supportive secondary endpoints.'
events.magnitude: The September 18 $15 straddle marked about $17.20—roughly ±118% around $14.53. Because the downside cannot go below zero and spreads remain wide, this is proof of extreme skew, not a probabilistic forecast.
events.action: Pre-register the scorecard: primary endpoint, effect size, p-value, missing data, subgroup consistency, safety/discontinuations, secondary endpoints, and whether FDA still requires a second pivotal study.
events.invalidation: Company moves topline beyond August or the ESC presentation no longer contains LEVEL results.
events.watch: Topline release date, database lock, exact primary endpoint and effect size, ESC abstract details, FDA meeting guidance, cash runway, and financing language.
events.plain_summary: TENX expects major trial results in August for a heart-and-lung treatment.
events.plain_good: Strong results could support approval and attract a partner.
events.plain_bad: Weak or failed results could erase much of the company’s drug value.
events.plain_watch: Watch the size of the benefit, safety, and whether FDA still wants another large trial.

context: Sector mix: four Health Care events and four non-healthcare events across Communications/Space, Materials/Defense Supply Chain, Consumer/IP, and Financials/M&A.
Seven of eight names are below $10B; ASTS is retained despite its larger market value because three satellites on one mission create a real operational discontinuity.
Lower-confidence non-healthcare windows are explicitly labeled. MP is an operating-update catalyst, ASTS is a launch window, TWO is a closing window, and CRCT is a confirmed agency target date.
Option ranges use July 24 marks. CRCT had no defensible two-sided option market; ASTS, MP, and TWO ranges carry the stated liquidity and structural caveats.
methodology: Scan the rolling 42-day market for one-ticker discontinuities, then enforce at least four sectors and no more than four events from any one sector. Prefer sub-$10B names and primary-source dates, but admit lower-confidence windows when they add real sector diversity. For every candidate, separate source/date confidence from trade probability; map exact trigger, white/base/black paths, mispricing, invalidation, market-cap/reference context, and defensible option evidence or an explicit “not defensible.”
